summary: The change sends every GitHub-agent error check through errorText, as the checker's checks already did: gather, post, both push-and-reply sites, snapshot, the PR description update, the finish comment and both record steps. A '""', "''" or null from a model now counts as empty everywhere, and a real error still stops the run. Tracing the new loop-test scenarios by reading (they were not run here) shows both cases: the #790 shape now reaches the handoff and the record commit, and a real description error still stops at finish. No correctness bug was found. The one finding asks whether these eight per-site calls are what issue #42 meant by normalizing once at parse time.

findings.title: errorText is applied at eight call sites, not once at parse time as #42 asks
findings.description: Issue #42 is titled "Normalize every agent's error field once, at parse time", and the branch name says the same. The PR does something different. It calls errorText at each of the eight GitHub-agent check sites (gather 1345, post 1399, push-and-reply 1533 and 1792, snapshot 1691, finish 1913 and 1925, record 1943 and 1961). run() (227-233) still returns the raw `error`. Any new agent call written as `if (out.error)` will stop the run the way Losers League #790 did. The loop test covers only the PR description site, so a revert at any of the other seven sites would go unnoticed. The thrown messages also use the raw `.error`, not the normalized text. errorText still sits under the "The checker's verdict" section header, and the empty-text rule is still written for the checker only in agent-os/standards/workflow/agents.md:17 and README.md:232. Question for the person: normalize once in run(), as the issue title says, or keep the per-site calls? The trade-off: normalizing in run() changes the stored error, including what `detail.checker` keeps (README.md:232 says it keeps whatever the checker returned) and the post warning text. The per-site calls keep the raw value but depend on every future call site remembering errorText.
findings.proposedFix: Option A (once, at parse time): in run(), after the null check, add `if (typeof out === 'object' && typeof out.error === 'string') { out.error = errorText(out) }`. Move errorText next to run(). The per-site calls then become plain truthiness tests. One loop-test scenario with error '""' on another GitHub call (post or push-and-reply) would then show the rule holds beyond the description update. Note in README.md:232 that detail.checker now holds the normalized text. Option B (keep per-site): move errorText out of the checker section to the helpers near run(). Add a line to agent-os/standards/workflow/agents.md saying every agent's error is read through errorText, and widen README.md:232 to match. Add '""' scenarios for at least post (no warning on a consistent review) and push-and-reply.
